g.text: ADR-007: What the public sees, and what only staff see
Status: accepted
Session: —
Cards: —
Exam: —
Supersedes: none
Superseded by: none
Question
one sentence
Which data does TrialWatch show to anyone, and which only to its admins and moderators, now that the web interface can be served to the
public?
Context
what forces this decision now: facts and constraints, no solutions
• ADR-006 let anyone browse every page: unreviewed model judgements, their traces (prompts, raw answers), sources and transfers, gold labels with false-
accusation flags, and staff emails in the history.
• A judgement says a sponsor did not report fully: public, it is an accusation. A model can misread a page, so a wrong one harms a sponsor and our
credibility.
• The methodology should stay open: how we check (requirement sets, prompts, run settings) is what makes a result trustworthy.
• Staff are people: their emails are personal data and nobody outside needs them.
• ADR-001 proposed manual approval below 99% confidence; we have no calibrated confidence yet.
• Revision 2026-11-22: transparency comes first. If our check decides the evidence is not enough, that is published as it is, with how far checks of its
kind can be trusted, not held back until a person agrees.
Options
2–3 real options; the current proposal is only one of them
A. Everything public, mark drafts
How it works: all pages stay open; unreviewed
judgements carry a "draft" badge.
+ nothing to build
– a draft accusation is still public and indexed
– traces and emails stay public
B. Publish step and a staff view
How it works: checks.publication records what is
public; a withdrawn one stays public, marked.
Revised 2026-11-22: a run publishes every
judgement it made without an error, any label,
with how often judgements of its kind agreed
with gold labels (the share once ≥ 20 items, the
basis always). The public sees each published
judgement with its whole trace; staff also see
sources, gold, run tallies, costs and names.
+ everything we decide is open, with its method
+ a withdrawal can't hide a result
– a misread page is a public accusation until
staff withdraw it
C. Sign-in for everyone
How it works: a viewer role; nothing is public.
+ simplest to reason about
– defeats a public watchdog
– accounts to manage for every reader
Criteria × options
+ better · 0 no difference · – worse, and a few words why
Criterion
Option A
Option B
Option C
Harm: wrong accusation public
– drafts are public
– all public, agreement shown
+ nothing public
Openness: method and results
+ everything
+ results and the whole trace
– nothing without an account
Privacy: staff names
– emails public
+ shown as staff
0 readers see them
Effort: build and run
+ none
+ one table, filters, no review
– accounts for readers
Undo: how hard to reverse later
+ drop one table and view
Decision
what we chose and which criteria decided it
We choose B, revised 2026-11-22 for transparency. Every judgement without an error is published by its run as it finishes, any label, however often its
kind agreed with gold. A kind (model, prompt text, requirement set, label, quotes verified, asked again with every page, a question unanswered) is
compared with gold labels; the publication records the share once ≥ 20 items were compared, and its basis always (checks/publishing.py). Nobody publishes
by hand. Staff may withdraw one with a reason (judgement.withdraw); it stays public, marked withdrawn with the reason. Public (view.published): published
judgements with their whole trace (questions, pages read, prompt and message sent, raw answers, quote checks, rules), their runs, prompts, requirement
sets and the files they quote, listed on the home page with filters. Staff only: the full trial and sponsor lists, judgements of running or failed checks,
sources and transfers, gold, run tallies, costs, the workflow and names. Decided by openness over harm: gold agreement is shown with each result, not used
as a gate.
Consequences
Easier: no review queue; everything we decide is public with its
method, and a withdrawal can't hide a result.
Harder: a misread page is a public accusation until staff withdraw
it; readers must weigh the gold agreement shown with each result.
Revisit when · Lab
Revisit when: a kind with low gold agreement keeps publishing
accusations; sponsors should be told before publication; a public API
or export is wanted.
Lab: tests/test_publication.py (a run publishes, the public trace, a
withdrawal stays public with its reason, staff-only pages, names, files)
and test_publishing.py (every label published, agreement recorded).
Session notes
optional
Decided with the user on 2026-11-21: the public is anyone; the public sees verdict and quotes, not the trace; gold and sources are staff only; runs,
prompts and history stay public. Then: approve by hand below 90% confidence, measured on gold; above it any label, accusations included, publishes by
itself (replacing ADR-001's 99% proposal).
Revised with the user on 2026-11-22: publish everything, even judgements whose kind disagrees with gold; show the public the whole trace; keep
withdraw, shown with its reason; drop /review. Replaced: the 90% gate, publishing by hand (judgement.publish), and hiding the trace from the public.
How to use: copy to docs/adr/ADR-NNN-name.excalidraw · replace the grey text (set it to black) · status chip colour: orange open, yellow proposed, green accepted, grey
superseded · one page: if it doesn't fit, the decision is too big, so split it.
